name: Albert Schweitzer Foundation: 2016 estimate (ACE)
summary: Campaigns for farmed animals in Germany and beyond, through corporate outreach, lobbying, consumer outreach and media work. Animal Charity Evaluators' 2016 Guesstimate model: projected costs and achievements by program, converted here by species into chicken-equivalent pain days per dollar, like our other animal models: hens spared cages as hen-years of a caged hen's suffering, other animals spared with the shared figure per animal. ACE has since stopped publishing per-dollar estimates; this is the last public one for this charity.

sections.title: Model
sections.explainer:
The Albert Schweitzer Foundation provided budget and accomplishments information for 2015 and partial information for January to August 2016. Estimates in this sheet are made by Animal Charity Evaluators for the full year of 2016.

Read ACE's 2016 [review](https://animalcharityevaluators.org/research/charity-review/albert-schweitzer-foundation/) of the Albert Schweitzer Foundation.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: charityevals adjustments on top of ACE's model.

sections.title: Discounting
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not ACE's. ACE counts a year of benefit the same whenever it comes. In our view, later years count less at the discount rate under Your values, as in GiveWell's models; the evaluator view sets the rate to 0, so ACE's numbers reproduce.

sections.title: In chicken pain days
sections.explainer: charityevals' step, not ACE's. ACE's 2016 models count years of farmed-animal life spared, every species alike. Here hens spared cages count as years of a caged hen's suffering, and every other animal spared by the shared figure for an animal spared, split by species like a replaced meal. Each species is then counted in days of a chicken's disabling pain (Rethink Priorities' estimates); how a chicken compares with a person is the chicken slider.

rows.label: Total years of suffering spared per dollar
Staff pay as a share of program cost
rows.explainer: Advocacy is mostly people, so staff pay is usually most of the budget. We haven't seen this charity's breakdown; the default is the same guess we use for other animal advocacy groups. Range is ours.

rows.label: Pay gap versus comparable jobs elsewhere
rows.explainer: Campaigners, researchers and negotiators could typically earn considerably more in comparable for-profit roles. Range is ours.

rows.label: Share of the full cost paid by cash donations
rows.explainer: With credit by share of resources, staff's forgone pay counts as part of the cost, and staff get their share of the outcome. Off, this is 100%.

rows.label: Participants in Vegan Taste Week program
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 42000 to 63000 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF provided: "In 2015, 49,293 people signed up for the Vegan Taste Week and in the first eight months of 2016, 39,187 people signed up."

rows.label: Local action groups
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 30 to 38 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF provided: "In 2015, we were able to grow the net number of local groups by 7 and in 2016, we increased it by another 7 during the first eight months, now totalling 37 groups." Their [website](https://albert-schweitzer-stiftung.de/helfen/aktiv) lists the groups and their planned activities. While some do not have activities listed, they may be active more infrequently; however it is also possible that some groups with no listed activities have dissolved and ASF is not yet aware of this.

rows.label: Leaflets distributed
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 350000 to 480000 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF provided: "In 2015, we distributed 444,533 brochures and in 2016, we have distributed 311,340 brochures, so far (with one major push coming later this year)." 

Some channels of distribution (such as through local groups or by mail to activist who order them to distribute) may result in ASF overestimating the number of leaflets distributed to the public, if not all the leaflets they ship are distributed.

rows.label: Visitors to the Vegan Summer Festival
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 45000 to 65000 (normal). The best guess is its median.

ASF provided: "The Vegan Summer Festival is co-hosted every year by VEBU, Berlin Vegan and Albert Schweitzer Foundation. It runs for three days and attracted 55,000 visitors in 2015 and 60,000 visitors in 2016."

rows.label: Newsletter subscribers
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 95000 to 110000 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF provided: "Our weekly newsletter reached 100,000 subscribers in August 2016."

This metric doesn’t directly figure into our cost-effectiveness calculations because the subscribers are already accounted for in the figures of people reached by ASF outreach.

rows.label: Animals spared per leaflet
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, .21 to 1.86 (normal). The best guess is its median.

Derived from our [leafleting calculator](http://www.animalcharityevaluators.org/research/interventions/impact-calculator/). Does not include shellfish or wild fish.

As of 2011, Germans typically eat [about 75%](http://faostat3.fao.org/download/FB/CL/E) as much meat as people in the US, so since the calculator was developed from US data, we multiplied its outputs by .75.

The same figure is kept as shared data (Animal Charity Evaluators, under Data), which this row reads.

rows.label: Years of suffering spared per leaflet
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, .079 to .5 (normal). The best guess is its median.

Derived from our [leafleting calculator](http://www.animalcharityevaluators.org/research/interventions/impact-calculator/). Does not include shellfish or wild fish.

As of 2011, Germans typically eat [about 75%](http://faostat3.fao.org/download/FB/CL/E) as much meat as people in the US, so since the calculator was developed from US data, we multiplied its outputs by .75.

The same figure is kept as shared data (Animal Charity Evaluators, under Data), which this row reads.

rows.label: Animals spared per participant
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 1 to 40 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

We assume that the program is about 1/4 as effective per participant as [Veganuary](https://www.getguesstimate.com/models/7225)'s month-long pledge program. This is an extremely crude assumption, so we incorporate additional uncertainty at both ends of the range.

rows.label: Years of suffering spared per participant
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, .4 to 11 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

Different animals have wildly different lifespans in industrial agriculture systems, ranging from a few weeks for broiler chickens to several years for cows used in milk production.

Since the Vegan Taste Week pledge program addresses overall consumption of animal products in a similar way to leafleting programs, the ratio between animals spared and years of suffering spared should be similar for the two programs. We used this fact, our estimates for the impact of leafleting seen in other cost-effectiveness models, and the number of animals spared per participant calculated for the pledge program to arrive at an appropriate range of years of suffering spared

rows.label: Animals spared per dollar by consumer outreach
rows.explainer: We measure the effects of consumer outreach by adding together the effects from leaflets distributed and Vegan Taste Week participation. We do not account separately for the effects of local groups (which have at least some of their effectiveness through these two outcomes) or visitors to the Vegan Summer Festival (which we do not adequately understand).

rows.label: Years of suffering spared per dollar by consumer outreach
rows.explainer: We measure the effects of consumer outreach by adding together the effects from leaflets distributed and Vegan Taste Week participation. We do not account separately for the effects of local groups (which have at least some of their effectiveness through these two outcomes) or visitors to the Vegan Summer Festival (which we do not adequately understand).

rows.label: Corporate policy victories
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 25 to 40 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF provided: "In 2015, we convinced 31 companies to go cage-free and in the first eight months of 2016, we convinced 17 companies to do so.... After a quick campaign to get German supermarkets to stop selling eggs from caged quails, we developed a relationship with Europe’s largest quail producer, Urgasa.... In 2014, the federal state of Lower Saxony announced that it will outlaw beak searing by the end of 2016. In 2015 and 2016, basically all other decision makers such as the German Agriculture Minister and the egg industry agreed to end the practice by 2016/2017....Late in 2015, a leading German retailer decided to cooperate with us on better trout welfare in aquaculture....One of the most prominent signs of success in that area is the fact that we are cooperating closely with several supermarket chains in order to produce and refine their animal welfare policies. We were able to make meaningful contributions to two policies, gave detailed ex-post feedback to two additional chains that will be considered in the next updates, and are now working on an update with another chain....In 2015, we worked with 34 companies and dining operations to generate 46 impact points (relating to providing mainstream vegan options) and in 2016 we, so far, have worked with 6 companies to generate 41 impact points."

rows.label: Hens affected yearly by cage-free policies ASF was involved with
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 600000 to 40000000 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF did not provide an estimate, leading us to have considerable uncertainty. We used ASF's estimate of 65 million hens affected by debeaking policies set to affect all eggs sold in Germany as an upper bound. On the lower bound, the vast majority of estimates for the number of hens affected by policy changes by individual grocery chains in the US are larger than 100,000. While Germany is smaller than the US, many of those estimates were for regional chains, so we think it's unlikely that the policies reported by ASF will affect fewer than 1 million hens in total.

rows.label: Animals affected yearly by other policy changes ASF was involved with
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 60000000 to 100000000 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

The 65 million hens ASF says will be affected by an end to debeaking in Germany provide a lower bound. We are very uncertain about the scope of some of the other policy changes they have cited, but none seem clearly larger in reach than that change.

rows.label: Proportional improvement in welfare due to cage-free policies
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, -.25 to .46 (normal). The best guess is its median.

Hens suffer in both battery cage and cage-free systems. While many advocates believe that cage-free systems are better from the hen's perspective, some disagree. Most research privileges outcomes of interest to farmers, rather than the hens' interests.

rows.label: Proportional improvement in welfare due to other policies
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, -.24 to .33 (normal). The best guess is its median.

Other policies ASF has mentioned include ending debeaking, ending caged quail farming, improving "transport, hygiene, antibiotics use, water quality, slaughter, inspecting carcasses at slaughter, expertise of workers" in trout farming, and broad animal welfare policies adopted by retailers. 

Some policies, such as debeaking, have possible downsides for animals.

We think the debeaking policy here is likely the one which will affect the most animals. As with cage-free policies, while many think it is positive on balance, if it is implemented poorly there is a risk that hens will wound each other due to the conditions of farming.

rows.label: ASF's responsibility for changes
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, .3 to .8 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF is a leading group when it comes to corporate outreach in Germany, but The Humane League has driven some of the push toward cage-free policies internationally and was involved in some of ASF's victories. Other groups may also have been involved.

rows.label: ASF's responsibility for changes
rows.explainer:
Beta(7, 3) in Guesstimate: best guess is its mean, range its 90% interval.

ASF is a leader in corporate outreach in Germany. While we're not aware of specific roles played by other groups in these victories, some are sweeping enough that we think other groups may have played a supporting role.

rows.label: Years of impact expected
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 1 to 15 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

We consider a limited term of impact because companies might simply have adopted the same policy later without ASF's influence, might go out of business, or might abandon the policy after following it for some number of years.

rows.label: Discount rate on future benefits
rows.explainer: The shared discount rate (Your values). ACE's 2016 model doesn't discount, so the evaluator view pins it at 0.

rows.label: Same rate, compounded continuously
rows.explainer: The yearly rate as a continuous rate, so benefits spread over years can be discounted smoothly rather than in yearly steps.

rows.label: Years of impact expected, discounted
rows.explainer: ACE multiplies the animals a policy affects each year by the years of impact, counting every year the same. In our view later years count less at the discount rate: this is the present value of one animal-year per year over that many years (equal to the years at a 0% rate; 3.6 instead of 3.9 at 4%).

rows.label: Equivalent hens spared from cage-free policies
Equivalent years of suffering spared from cage-free policies
rows.explainer: Since laying hens typically live for 1-2 years, the number of hens affected yearly is approximately the number of years of suffering reduced yearly (but we must correct for the fact that these hens are not spared from all the suffering involved in industrial agriculture). (A hen who lives for two years will be considered "affected yearly" for both of them, so does not need to be counted twice here.)

rows.label: Equivalent animals spared from other policies
Equivalent years of suffering spared from other policies
rows.explainer: We expect many of the animals affected to be laying hens and trout, and since laying hens and farmed fish typically live for 1-2 years, the number of these animals affected yearly is approximately the number of years of suffering reduced yearly (but we must correct for the fact that these they are not spared from all the suffering involved in industrial agriculture). (An animal who lives for two years will be considered "affected yearly" for both of them, so does not need to be counted twice here.) However, some animals affected by the broader policies will likely live for shorter periods.

Articles written by scientific department
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 24 to 40 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF provided: "In 2015, our scientific department staff wrote 37 articles for our websites and in 2016, it has written 24 articles, so far."

rows.label: Books citing ASF's articles
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 6 to 9 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF provided: "Nine of these articles were cited in five books in 2015 and 16 have been cited in six books in 2016, so far."

rows.label: Presentations and articles prepared for influential groups
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 16 to 35 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF provided: "In 2015, we gave 14 presentations, seminars and panel discussions to these target groups. In the first eight months of 2016, that number was eight. 

We are also writing articles and giving interviews to media that is especially consumed by influencers and experts (14 in 2015 and 8 in 2016, so far)."

They also specifically cited some other presentations and conference organizing which we think are relevant here and may not have been counted in this number

rows.label: Monthly engaged users (Facebook)
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 83000 to 113000 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF's Facebook reports show an average of 98151 engaged users (anyone who clicks, comments on, shares, or reacts to the page) in a 28 day period. Estimated error due to variation over time is +/- 15%.

rows.label: Yearly unique video views to 95% (Facebook)
rows.explainer:
ACE's 90% interval, 123000 to 167000 (lognormal). The best guess is its median.

ASF's Facebook reports show 72475 unique views to 95% over 180 days. This leads to our mean estimate of 144950 unique views to 95% per year, with error due to changes over time of +/- 15%.

rows.label: Animals spared per dollar by social media
rows.explainer:

Estimated using our [social media calculator](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1jzsw9Suc8HHpzRPeaVDK4oMqQoFTH12HtXYeaW4SrVk/edit#gid=1263869078) for ASF.

rows.explainer: The same chickens, counted as ACE counts animals spared, so they aren't counted again among other animals.

rows.label: Other animals spared per dollar
rows.explainer: Every other animal ACE counts as spared, mostly through diet change. ACE's 2016 sheets don't say which species they are.

rows.label: SADs averted per animal spared
rows.explainer: The shared figures for a replaced meal, in suffering-adjusted days (SADs) and in animals, give the suffering behind each animal spared: about 8.7 SADs. Every model that counts animals spared uses this one rate, split by species. ACE's 2016 sheets don't give a species breakdown, so the split is ACE's 2024 estimate of which animals a plant-based diet spares.

rows.label: Chicken-equivalent pain days averted per dollar you give: chickens
rows.explainer: The SADs for chickens with Ambitious Impact's weight for a hen (46% of a person's) taken out, which leaves days of a chicken's disabling pain. A chicken counts as 1 here by definition; how a chicken's suffering compares with a person's is the chicken slider. The evaluator view keeps Ambitious Impact's weight, so ACE's own result reproduces.
